title: When the Verdict Wakes
premise: Astrid Hartwell, concierge at the Saltmere Grand, has spent three years quietly cataloguing the secrets of a coastal town still haunted by the disappearance of schoolteacher Maren Voss. When Maren's diary surfaces in the hotel's lost-and-found with entries written after the date she vanished, Astrid realizes someone has been keeping her alive on paper — and that the diary's coded references point to an alibi network built thirty years earlier around another drowning. As Astrid and Detective Ilsa Brandt, torn between duty and growing love, follow the tide-line of evidence, they discover Maren staged her own disappearance to escape a powerful family's cover-up, but was silenced before she could leave. The verdict that finally wakes is Astrid's own: she must choose between protecting the town's fragile peace and publishing the truth, and in doing so finds the found family she never filed away.
about_author: Ada Nystrom is a former night-desk receptionist who spent a decade collecting the confessions strangers make to people behind front desks. She writes mysteries set in small coastal towns where everyone knows your name and no one knows your business.

chapters.title: The Lost and Found Ledger
chapters.summary: POV: Astrid. While alphabetizing the hotel's lost-and-found, Astrid discovers Maren Voss's diary — and freezes: entries continue three weeks past her disappearance date. The final entry names 'the boathouse at low tide.' Emotional beat: the quiet archivist's ordered world cracks open; curiosity overrides three years of deliberate neutrality.

chapters.title: Thirty Years of Alibis
chapters.summary: POV: Astrid. Astrid cross-references the diary against old guest ledgers and realizes the same five families checked in every anniversary week for decades. Detective Ilsa Brandt arrives investigating a fresh break-in at the Voss house. Emotional beat: wary alliance — two women who notice everything, each hiding what they've noticed.

chapters.title: What the Tide Keeps
chapters.summary: POV: Ilsa. At the boathouse, Ilsa and Astrid find a hidden waterproof case: photographs from 1994 showing a teenage boy drowning during a party hosted by the Aldergate family — and Maren, then a student, watching. Emotional beat: dread hardening into purpose; the past isn't buried, it's moored.

chapters.title: The Anniversary Guests
chapters.summary: POV: Astrid. The five families arrive for their annual gathering, and Astrid works the front desk like a listening post, cataloguing lies. One guest, elderly Henrik Aldergate, asks pointedly whether anything 'of Maren's' ever turned up. Emotional beat: Astrid learns the thrill and terror of holding leverage.

chapters.title: Entries After the End
chapters.summary: POV: Ilsa. Forensics confirms the late diary entries are in Maren's hand but written recently — someone with access to her handwriting. Suspicion falls on Maren's reclusive sister, Runa, who once worked for the Aldergates. Emotional beat: Ilsa's duty pulls toward an easy suspect while her instinct pulls toward Astrid.

chapters.title: Runa's Silence
chapters.summary: POV: Astrid. Runa finally speaks: Maren didn't vanish — she planned to, using Runa as her anchor. But Runa stopped receiving letters a year ago. Someone else has been writing the diary entries to keep the families returning, checking on them. Emotional beat: grief and betrayal; the found-family theme sharpens as Astrid vows not to abandon Runa.

chapters.title: Low Water
chapters.summary: POV: Ilsa. A storm drops the tide further than usual, exposing the wreck of the old Aldergate skiff — with human remains aboard, too degraded to be Maren. It's the 1994 boy. The alibi network wasn't hiding Maren's death; it was hiding his. Emotional beat: vertigo — every assumption collapses at once.

chapters.title: The Keeper of the Diary
chapters.summary: POV: Astrid. Astrid deciphers the diary's marginal codes and identifies the writer: the hotel's beloved retired owner, Edvard, Maren's secret ally, who kept the entries alive to slowly force the families into confession. But Henrik has realized it too. Emotional beat: heartbreak — the kindest man in town is both architect and target.

chapters.title: Verdict at High Tide
chapters.summary: POV: Ilsa and Astrid alternating. Henrik confronts Edvard at the cliffside boathouse; Astrid and Ilsa arrive as violence breaks out. Ilsa must arrest the town's patriarch with only Astrid's admissible testimony — choosing truth over the department's pressure to bury it. Emotional beat: climax; love against duty resolved as the same choice.

chapters.title: Filed Under New Names
chapters.summary: POV: Astrid. Weeks later, the trial opens old wounds and closes old accounts; Runa moves into the hotel, Edvard recovers, and Astrid retires her secret ledger, replacing it with a guest book full of real connections. The last diary entry reads simply: 'Tell them.' Emotional beat: resolution — loyalty to truth becomes belonging; the family she found was the one she stopped filing.
